The First Tax Year Sets Everything After It

A corporation chooses its own fiscal year-end. The first tax year starts on the incorporation date, and it may not exceed 53 weeks, which is a maximum of 371 days counted inclusively. Every month-end inside that window is available.

The choice is made on the first return and then stays. The Canada Revenue Agency holds the year-end on record, and a transmission is rejected when the dates sent do not match that record, so the year-end is worth getting right the first time rather than correcting later.

Each Year-End Carries Its Own Due Date

A T2 is due within six months of the fiscal year-end, so the year-end chosen also fixes every filing date that follows. The calculator shows the due date beside each permitted year-end, shifted to the next business day where it falls on a weekend or a statutory holiday.

A year with no activity is still a filing year, and the fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

A Short First Year Is Normal

Most first tax years are shorter than twelve months, because the year-end is chosen to suit the corporation rather than to fill a calendar year. A short first year is a complete tax year, needs its own T2, and does not reduce the fee.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can the Year-End Be Changed Later?

Not freely. A fiscal year-end already on record with the Canada Revenue Agency cannot be moved without the Agency agreeing to the change, which is why the first return matters.

Why Does the Calculator Only Show Month-Ends?

Because almost every corporation uses one, and a month-end keeps the year-end stable from year to year. A year-end mid-month is permitted and the 53-week limit is the same; ask us if that is what you need.

Is the Longest First Year Always the Best?

No. A longer first year delays the first return but moves every later due date with it. The calculator shows both effects so the trade is visible rather than guessed at.

Does a First Year With No Activity Still Need a Return?

Yes. The obligation follows the existence of the corporation, not its activity. A first year in which nothing happened is filed at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

What Else Is Due in the First Year?

A first return also carries Schedule 24. A federally incorporated corporation separately files its annual return with Corporations Canada within 60 days of its anniversary, which is a $12.00 government fee and is not part of the T2.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What This Checker Decides, and What It Does Not

This checker answers one question: is a nil T2 the return you need, and can this service file it. It is deliberately narrow. The four gates are the kind of return, whether the year has ended, whether the year was nil, and whether it is already filed.

It does not grade how nil the year was. That is the dormant corporation test, which asks ten activity questions and names the item that disqualifies the year. Use this one to find out whether to start, and that one to find out whether the year itself qualifies.

What Makes a Year Nil

A nil tax year is one in which the corporation carried on no business, earned nothing and paid nothing out. The corporation can still exist, hold a bank account and own assets.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

What Happens When the Answer Is Yes

The fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. You give the corporation details, pick the tax years, pay, confirm the filing information and sign Form T183CORP on a secure single-use screen. Your return is transmitted electronically by a registered EFILE electronic filer and your CRA confirmation is emailed within 3 business days.

Frequently Asked Questions

What If More Than One Year Is Outstanding?

Check the oldest one here, then use the unfiled years checker to list every year still outstanding and what each one was due.

The Corporation Has Never Traded at All. Does It Still File?

Yes. A corporation that was incorporated and never started operating files a T2 for every tax year until it is formally dissolved.

What If the Year Turns Out Not to Be Nil After I Pay?

We check before you pay. If we find it afterwards, we refund you in full, and the work is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca instead.

Does an Open GST/HST Account Change the Answer?

Not for the T2. It does mean that account has its own nil filings or an RC145 closure, which the GST/HST nil filing checker covers.

Is a Nil T2 a Shorter Form?

No. It is a complete T2 with the figures at zero. The identification, the fiscal year dates and the GIFI schedules where they are required are all still part of the return.

title: Unfiled Years Checker | Which T2 Years Are Outstanding
content:

Your year-ends

Enter your first fiscal year-end and the outstanding years appear here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Return Per Tax Year, Oldest First

There is no combined return covering several years. Each outstanding tax year is its own T2, with its own fiscal year dates and its own due date six months after that year-end.

They are filed oldest first, because each year’s closing position carries into the next return. Filing out of order means going back over earlier years.

Why an Open Year Matters When Nothing Was Owed

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

That is the whole reason to catch up a nil year: not a bill, but a year that stays open and a file that cannot be closed.

What the Catch-Up Costs

Every year costs the same, $300.00 plus HST per tax year, whether it is current or years late. There is no hourly billing and no surcharge for a late year. The unfiled years cost calculator turns a year count into the total.

Frequently Asked Questions

What If I Do Not Know My First Fiscal Year-End?

It is on your first notice of assessment, and your corporate tax account in My Business Account lists each tax year on record. The fiscal year end calculator shows which month-ends a first year could have used.

I Have Never Filed Anything. What Do I Enter?

Leave the second date blank. Every tax year that has ended is then listed as outstanding, starting from the first year-end.

Does the Checker Look at My CRA Account?

No. It works only from the two dates you type, so it cannot see what the Canada Revenue Agency has on record. Treat the list as the years to ask about, not as a statement of your account.

How Many Years Can Be Filed at Once?

There is no limit. Years are prepared together and transmitted oldest first, one return per tax year, each with its own Form T183CORP.

What If One of Those Years Was Not Nil?

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

title: Non-Resident T2 Penalty Calculator | $25.00 a Day to $2,500.00
content:
Penalty Tool

Non-Resident T2 Penalty Calculator

For a non-resident-owned corporation, a late T2 costs $25.00 per day to a maximum of $2,500.00. Enter the dates and the calculator counts it.

$25.00 per dayMaximum $2,500.00Cap reached on day 100Non-resident-owned corporations

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Your dates

Enter the due date and the figure appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Who This Figure Applies To

This calculator is for a corporation owned by non-residents of Canada. For that corporation a late T2 carries a day-count charge of $25.00 per day, to a maximum of $2,500.00, which is reached on day 100 and does not grow after it.

A corporation owned by residents of Canada filing a true nil return is in a different position, and the block below is the whole of it.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Working Out the Due Date First

The figure depends entirely on the due date, which is six months after the fiscal year-end, shifted to the next business day where it lands on a weekend or a statutory holiday. The nil T2 deadline calculator works that date out from a year-end, and the unfiled years checker lists it for every outstanding year at once.

The Count Stops When the Return Is Filed

The day count runs to the filing date, so it stops on the day the return is transmitted. Filing a nil year that is already past the cap does not reduce the charge, but it does close the year, which is what unblocks a clearance certificate and a dissolution.

A nil T2 is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is This the Same as the Percentage Late-Filing Charge?

No. The percentage charge is calculated on tax owing, so on a true nil return it is $0.00. The $25.00 a day is a separate day-count charge stated for a non-resident-owned corporation.

What Counts as Non-Resident-Owned?

That depends on who holds the shares and where they are resident, and it is a determination Sharad Gondaliya, CPA, makes on the file rather than something a calculator should decide. Use the figure here once you know the corporation is in that position.

Does the Maximum Reset Each Year?

Each tax year is its own return with its own due date, so the day count and the maximum are worked out per year. Six late years are six separate counts, not one.

Will Filing Now Remove the Charge?

Filing stops the day count at the filing date. It does not erase the days already counted, and we never promise an outcome on a charge the Canada Revenue Agency assesses.

Does the Calculator Include Interest?

No. It counts only the day-count charge at $25.00 a day to $2,500.00. Interest is a separate calculation on an amount owing, and a true nil return has none.

title: Dissolution Readiness Checker | Before You Wind Up
content:
Closing Check

Dissolution Readiness Checker

Four questions in the order the steps actually run, naming the first one still outstanding before a corporation is dissolved.

Four steps in orderNames the first gapReturns come before clearanceAccounts closed last

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 26, 2026

Four questions about where the file stands

Answer all four and the result appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Steps Run in One Order

Dissolution is not a single filing. Four things happen, and they happen in this order, because each one depends on the one before it.

StepWhat it is
1Every outstanding T2 year filed
2The final T2 filed to the dissolution date
3A clearance certificate requested
4The Business Number programme accounts closed

An open tax year blocks a clearance certificate, which is why the returns are first and not last.

Two Different Bodies, Two Different Filings

Dissolving the corporation and closing its tax accounts are separate acts with separate bodies. The dissolution goes through the registry the corporation was incorporated with, federally through Corporations Canada or provincially. The returns and the account closures go to the Canada Revenue Agency.

Doing one without the other is the common failure: a corporation dissolved at the registry while an open tax year sits at the Agency can still be reassessed on that year.

What the Final Return Covers

The final T2 runs from the start of that fiscal year to the dissolution date, and it is due within six months of dissolution. It is required even when the closing year had no activity at all, and a nil final return is $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a Corporation Be Dissolved With Years Still Unfiled?

The registry and the Agency are separate, so a dissolution can be registered while years are open, but it leaves a dissolved corporation that can still be reassessed and a clearance certificate that cannot be settled. Filing first is what finishes the file.

How Many Years Might Be Outstanding?

Use the unfiled years checker to list every tax year still outstanding and what each one was due.

Is the Final Return Different From a Normal One?

It covers a shorter period, from the start of the fiscal year to the dissolution date, and that period is what makes it final. A nil final return is otherwise an ordinary nil T2.

What Closes the GST/HST and Payroll Accounts?

Form RC145 closes the Business Number programme accounts, once each of those accounts has its own final return or remittance in.

What If the Corporation Held Assets?

Then the closing year is not nil. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.
